name: Ava AI
task: AI voice agents that answer for you
summary: AI phone agent for Shopify stores: answers support calls 24/7 — order lookup, edits and refunds mid-call — and runs outbound abandoned-cart recovery calls, with recordings, transcripts and its own business number. Priced by call minutes.
best_for: Shopify DTC and cash-on-delivery stores with real inbound call volume that want 24/7 phone support and outbound cart-recovery automated, and are comfortable with per-minute economics
skip_if: low-call-volume or thin-margin stores where per-minute overage can dwarf the base fee, and anyone who needs a proven track record — the review base is tiny (six) and the app is under a year old
honest_knock: The monthly price is a minutes allowance, not a flat fee — every minute past the bucket bills at $0.07 to $0.10, so a busy support line can cost far more than the headline. And keep the vendor's marketing at arm's length: Ava launched in September 2025 with just six App Store reviews, and the promoted 21–24x ROAS figures are the vendor's own, not independently verified. There is no free plan, only a 7-day trial.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month, includes 100 call minutes, then $0.10 a minute overage
pricing.notes: (verified 2026-08-28 on apps.shopify.com/ava-ai and avasales.ai) Three paid tiers, no free plan, each with a 7-day trial. Support is $29 a month and includes 100 call minutes, then $0.10 a minute; Recover is $99 a month with 400 minutes and $0.08 over; Scale is $499 a month with 1,500 minutes and $0.07 over. The headline price is really a minutes bucket: a store with real call volume pays the overage, so cost tracks conversation length, not seats. Estimate your monthly call minutes before you compare — at heavy volume the effective bill can sit well above the tier price.

compare_with.name: Ringly.io
compare_with.why: Ringly and Ava both put an AI voice agent on a Shopify store's phone line; Ava leans into live order actions and outbound recovery with per-minute pricing, while alternatives like Ringly, CallFlows and Fin differ mainly on minute rates and how much they do beyond answering. Compare on expected call minutes, not sticker price
